content: New data shows public bodies paid private consultants £3.4bn last year, with government spending up £1.3bn (62%) compared with 2019-20 and still above pre-pandemic levels after the Covid-era spike. The figures highlight the challenge for Keir Starmer’s government, which has pledged to cut consultant spending by half during this parliament, even as major new contracts continue, including a KPMG deal worth up to £223m to train civil servants. Labour peer Prem Sikka condemned the reliance on consultants, arguing they add limited value and cannot quickly grasp and improve complex organisations. Is there anything else I can help with?.
